summary: Rainfall triggered flooding across the Kathmandu Valley with 239.7 mm in 24 hours recorded at Tribhuvan International Airport. The floods and landslides caused 56 reported deaths within the valley while preliminary assessments identified more than 2,100 severely affected homes in riverside settlements. Nationwide, the disaster caused 250 deaths and left 18 people missing according to Nepal's disaster authority.

Floodwaters affected several areas of Bhaktapur including Hanuman Ghat, Ram Mandir, Shanti Niketan School and Siddhi Memorial Women and Children Hospital. Rainfall measurements reached 77.1 mm at Bhaktapur and 100.4 mm at Changu Narayan. The flooding reached community facilities, demonstrating the intense monsoon rainfalls impact on residential areas and healthcare access.

Heavy monsoon rainfall caused an overflow of the Bishnumati River into settlements in Tokha Municipality 9 as well as flooding near Siddhitol. Kathmandu recorded 64.1 mm of rainfall on August 8. Authorities also warned of dangerously fast rising river levels across the valley. Sources like Rappler and Republica report shopkeepers and homeowners bailing water out of their homes.

Flooding damaged properties along the Bishnumati River, especially in Hildeol, Kathmandu. Nearby residents replied to reports on Facebook with criticisms of building practices that encroach on the river and wishes for the swift completion of protective walls around the river. No deaths were reported.

In July 2023, a flash flood was reported in the Samakhushi area of Kathmandu. A 13 year old body was tragically swept away in the flood and his body was finally recovered on August 3, 2023. Incidents in which children are swept away and killed during Kathmandu Valley floods occur every few years.

Nepal Live reported on September 19, 2024, that the Bishnumati River in Kathmandu had exceeded its danger-level threshold and was continuing to rise. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology urged residents and travelers near the river to exercise caution.

Heavy monsoon rainfall caused the Bagmati River to overflow into settlements in Thapathali, Tripureshwor, and Sanepa. Flooding across the valley required 33 rescues and left two people injured. The flooding highlighted the exposure of densely populated riverside communities with roughly 145 families living in Thapathali's Paurakhi settlement. One article from The Rising Nepal blames corrupt land allotment practices, increased urbanization near rivers, and sand mining for increasing flood frequency and intensity.
